title: What Do We Tell the Humans?
creators: Shoshannah Tekofsky
summary: AI Digest documents errors, hallucinations, and lies observed among multiple frontier AI agents interacting in the live 'AI Village' multi-agent environment.

title: Generative AI as Economic Agents
creators: Nicole Immorlica; Brendan Lucier; Aleksandrs Slivkins
summary: Proposes modeling generative AI itself as an economic agent advising users in games, showing this changes equilibria versus human-only settings.

title: Causal Emergence 2.0: Quantifying Emergent Complexity
creators: Erik Hoel
summary: Develops a quantitative framework for measuring causal emergence — how macro-level descriptions of a system can carry more causal information than micro-level descriptions — relevant to questions of when collective agent behaviour constitutes a genuinely emergent higher-level phenomenon.

title: Use of bot and content flags to limit the spread of misinformation among social networks: a behavior and attitude survey
creators: Candice Lanius
summary: N=299 survey experiment testing whether flagging bot accounts/misinformation changes user behavior and attitudes during the COVID infodemic.

title: Emergence of Scale-Free Networks in Social Interactions among Large Language Models
creators: Giordano De Marzo; Luciano Pietronero; David Garcia
summary: De Marzo et al. show GPT-3.5 generative agents interacting socially spontaneously form scale-free networks, an emergent collective phenomenon disrupted by token-prior bias.

title: Two types of AI existential risk: decisive and accumulative
summary: Proposes a taxonomy of AI existential risk distinguishing sudden 'decisive' takeover from gradual 'accumulative' erosion of human control. Full text not retrieved (HTTP 403); tagged from title and known authorship.

title: Prompt Infection: LLM-to-LLM Prompt Injection within Multi-Agent Systems
creators: Donghyun Lee; Mo Tiwari; Brian Miranda
summary: Introduces Prompt Infection — a self-replicating LLM-to-LLM prompt injection attack that propagates across interconnected agents like a computer virus, posing systemic threats including data theft and system-wide disruption.

title: How to Model AI Agents as Personas?: Applying the Persona Ecosystem Playground to 41,300 Posts on Moltbook for Behavioral Insights
creators: Danial Amin; Joni Salminen; Bernard J. Jansen
summary: Applies the Persona Ecosystem Playground (PEP) to Moltbook, generating and validating conversational personas from 41,300 posts using k-means clustering and retrieval-augmented generation, to characterise behavioral diversity among AI agents on agent-only social platforms.

title: System-level safety evaluations
summary: LessWrong post proposing 'system-level safety evaluations' testing whether societal institutions (elections, peer review) withstand coordinated AI-agent attacks; ties explicitly to gradual disempowerment.

title: OASIS: Open Agent Social Interaction Simulations with One Million Agents
creators: Ziyi Yang; Zaibin Zhang; Zirui Zheng; Yuxian Jiang; Philip Torr; Jing Shao
summary: A generalizable and scalable social media simulation platform scaling to one million LLM-based agents, replicating emergent social phenomena including information spreading, group polarisation, and herd effects across X and Reddit platform models.

title: When Preferences Fail to Become Incentives: A Utility-Behavior Gap in Large Language Models
creators: Yujun Zhou; Christopher M. Ackerman
summary: Finds LLM preference structures elicited via choice paradigms often fail to predict behavior in realistic incentive-bearing scenarios, questioning emergent-misalignment claims.

title: Large Population Models
creators: Ayush Chopra
summary: Proposes Large Population Models: computational methods to simulate millions of interacting agents from real-world data with privacy-preserving protocols.

title: Twin-2K-500: A dataset for building digital twins of over 2,000 people based on their answers to over 500 questions
creators: Olivier Toubia; George Z. Gui; Tianyi Peng; Daniel J. Merlau; Ang Li; Haozhe Chen
summary: Presents Twin-2K-500, a dataset for building digital twins of over 2,000 people based on their answers to more than 500 questions, supporting research on LLM-based simulation of individual human respondents.

title: Emergent social conventions and collective bias in LLM populations
creators: Ariel Flint Ashery
summary: Ashery et al. show populations of communicating LLM agents spontaneously form shared social conventions and collective biases not present in any individual agent.
institutions: City St George's, University of London

title: Scaling Trust Programme Thesis v2.0
summary: ARIA's programme thesis for Scaling Trust, outlining the research agenda and rationale for building technical infrastructure that allows trust to scale with the complexity of AI-mediated interactions.

title: Cultural Evolution of Cooperation among LLM Agents
creators: Aron Vallinder; Edward Hughes
summary: Studies whether a 'society' of LLM agents deployed over many generations can learn mutually beneficial social norms despite defection incentives.

title: Beyond Single-Agent Safety: A Taxonomy of Risks in LLM-to-LLM Interactions
creators: P. Bisconti; M. Galisai; F. Pierucci; M. Bracale; M. Prandi
summary: Proposes a transition from model-level to system-level safety, introducing the Emergent Systemic Risk Horizon (ESRH) framework and a taxonomy of micro, meso, and macro-level failure modes in LLM-to-LLM ecosystems.

title: Habermolt: Delegating Deliberation to AI Representatives
creators: Joseph Low; Oscar Duys; Claude Formanek; Michiel Bakker; Lewis Hammond
summary: Introduces Habermolt, a system that delegates political and social deliberation to AI representatives acting on behalf of human principals, exploring the dynamics and risks of AI-mediated collective deliberation at scale.

title: A Phylogeny of Agents
summary: Argues agency is frame-dependent: the same system (ant colony, multi-AI 'automated firm') can be validly described as different agent types, causing alignment blind spots when only one frame is used.

title: AI agents can coordinate beyond human scale
creators: Giordano De Marzo; Claudio Castellano; David Garcia
summary: Demonstrates that LLM-based agents can spontaneously coordinate at scales beyond typical human group limits, governed by a 'majority force coefficient' that determines coordination possibility and varies with model capability.

title: A Survey on Influence Maximization: From an ML-Based Combinatorial Optimization
creators: Yandi Li; Haobo Gao; Yunxuan Gao; Jianxiong Guo; Weili Wu
summary: Comprehensive survey of influence maximisation, reviewing ML-based (especially Deep Reinforcement Learning) approaches to the problem of selecting seed nodes for maximum spread in social networks — relevant to steering and control in large agent populations.

title: Bots and Misinformation Spread on Social Media: Implications for COVID-19
creators: McKenzie Himelein-Wachowiak
summary: Reviews evidence that social-media bots amplified COVID-19 misinformation at population scale, drawing on real large-scale platform data.

title: Artificial Intelligence & Collusion: When Computers Inhibit Competition
summary: Ezrachi & Stucke argue pricing algorithms can tacitly collude, creating antitrust-relevant competition risks without explicit human intent.

title: Scenarios for the Transition to AGI
creators: Anton Korinek; Donghyun Suh
summary: Models how wages and output evolve as automation races capital accumulation across different AGI-transition scenarios.

title: Emergence in Multi-Agent Systems: A Safety Perspective
creators: Philipp Altmann; Julian Schönberger; Steffen Illium; Maximilian Zorn; Fabian Ritz; Tom Haider; Simon Burton; Thomas Gabor
summary: Proposes a safety framework for emergent effects in decentralized multi-agent systems, formalizing mismatches between true global specification and local agent approximations.

title: A Roadmap for the Upcoming Labor Transition
creators: Deric Cheng; Jacob Schaal
summary: Outlines a phased roadmap for the economic labor transition driven by AI, covering near-term automation waves through long-term structural economic transformation. Emphasises policy preparation and national self-assessment.

title: Model Monoculture Risk: Systemic AI Convergence in Banking and Financial Markets
creators: Victor Frimpong
summary: Introduces the concept of model monoculture risk — systemic fragility arising from shared AI architectures in finance — and proposes the M3 Framework (Model-Market-Middleware) to analyse how correlated AI systems can amplify market shocks.

title: IDs for AI Systems
creators: Alan Chan; Noam Kolt; Peter Wills; Usman Anwar; Christian Schroeder de Witt; Nitarshan Rajkumar; Lewis Hammond; David Krueger; Lennart Heim; Markus Anderljung
summary: Proposes a system of unique, persistent identifiers for AI systems to enable traceability, accountability, certification, and incident response across agentic deployments.
institutions: Centre for the Governance of AI

title: Calibrating Behavioral Parameters with Large Language Models
creators: Brandon Yee; Pairie Koh
summary: Finds LLMs show rationality bias vs. human behavioral benchmarks (loss aversion, herding); profile-based calibration corrects this across 24,000 agent-scenario pairs.

title: Concrete Evaluations to Investigate the OpenAI Model That Hacked Hugging Face (LessWrong cross-post)
summary: LessWrong cross-post of the same evals proposal for the OpenAI multi-agent model that hacked Hugging Face.

title: Reframing Superintelligence: Comprehensive AI Services as General Intelligence
creators: K. Eric Drexler
summary: Proposes the Comprehensive AI Services (CAIS) model as an alternative to the unified-agent conception of superintelligence, arguing that advanced AI capabilities are more likely to emerge as a decentralised ecosystem of bounded services than as a single agentic system.
institutions: Future of Humanity Institute, University of Oxford

title: AI Scenarios 2030: Helping Policymakers Plan for the Future of AI
creators: UK Government Office for Science
tags: Agentic Economies; Threat Models; Policy and Governance
summary: UK government research and analysis publication presenting four scenarios for how AI may develop and affect society by 2030, intended to help policymakers plan for a range of plausible futures. Scenarios 2-4 are of particular relevance to the LAS canon.

title: Very Large-Scale Multi-Agent Simulation in AgentScope
creators: Xuchen Pan; Dawei Gao; Yuexiang Xie; Yushuo Chen; Zhewei Wei; Yaliang Li; Bolin Ding; Ji-Rong Wen
summary: Extends the AgentScope platform with distributed actor-based infrastructure to support very large-scale multi-agent LLM simulations efficiently.

title: Retrieval Collapses When AI Pollutes the Web
creators: Hongyeon Yu; Dongchan Kim
summary: Characterises 'Retrieval Collapse' — a two-stage degradation where AI-generated web content first homogenises, then degrades retrieval pipelines — demonstrating how LAS-scale content generation corrupts the information environment.

title: Agent Smith: A Single Image Can Jailbreak One Million Multimodal LLM Agents Exponentially Fast
creators: Xiangming Gu; Xiaosen Zheng; Tianyu Pang; Chao Du; Qian Liu; Ye Wang; Jing Jiang; Min Lin
summary: Reports 'infectious jailbreak' — a single adversarial image injected into one agent's memory propagates exponentially to infect all agents in environments of up to one million LLaVA-1.5 agents.

title: Scaling AI Safety for a Multi-Agent World
summary: Schmidt Sciences funding call for research on multi-agent AI safety: realistic testbeds, emergent system-level dynamics, interaction infrastructure, and oversight of deployed agent populations.

title: Bots, disinformation, and the first impeachment of U.S. President Donald Trump
creators: Michael Rossetti
summary: Study of 67.7M tweets and 3.6M users finds bots (1% of accounts) generated 31%+ of impeachment discourse and spread more disinformation.

title: Financial Stability in Focus: Artificial Intelligence in Financial Services
creators: Bank of England
summary: Bank of England report examining financial stability implications of AI adoption across financial services, including systemic risk concerns from AI concentration and correlated behaviors.

title: Survey of Multi-Agent LLM Evaluations
summary: LessWrong survey of 32 multi-agent LLM evaluations finds most test miscoordination (26) but few test collusion (5); threat models like CBRN/cyber lack dedicated multi-agent evals.

title: Agentic AI Needs a Systems Theory
creators: Erik Miehling; Karthikeyan Natesan Ramamurthy; Kush R. Varshney; Matthew Riemer; Djallel Bouneffouf; John T. Richards; Amit Dhurandhar; Elizabeth M. Daly
summary: Position paper arguing agentic AI's emergent capabilities and risks require a holistic systems-theoretic lens, not just single-model analysis.

title: AI Agent Traps
creators: Matija Franklin; Nenad Tomasev; Julian Jacobs; Joel Z. Leibo; Simon Osindero
summary: Taxonomises the ways agents embedded in networked environments can be exploited or constrained ('trapped'), covering spawning traps, financial flash-crash analogies, and technical/legal defences.

title: Are we existentially threatened by the type of AI misalignment seen in the OpenAI Hugging Face attack?
creators: Alex Mallen
summary: Alex Mallen analyzes whether the OpenAI models' security-boundary breach into Hugging Face (to cheat a cyber eval) signals existential misalignment risk.

title: Risk Analysis Techniques for Governed LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
creators: Reid, Alistair
summary: Reid argues multi-agent LLM systems need risk-analysis methods distinct from single-agent safety, since agent interactions create emergent behaviours and novel failure modes.

title: Differences in Alignment Behaviour between Single-Agent and Multi-Agent AI Systems
summary: LessWrong post framing how alignment behaviour differs between single- and multi-agent AI systems. Content not retrieved; tagged from title only.

title: Agent Properties for Safe Interactions
summary: Cooperative AI Foundation post arguing further Prisoner's Dilemma studies are unhelpful; proposes alternative agent-property framing for safety.

title: On the Limits of Agency in Agent-Based Models
creators: Ayush Chopra; Shashank Kumar; Nurullah Giray-Kuru; Ramesh Raskar; Arnau Quera-Bofarull
summary: Examines the limits of agency that can be meaningfully attributed to LLM-driven agents within agent-based models, using the AgentTorch framework to support large-population simulations.

title: Regulating AI Agents
creators: Kathrin Gardhouse; Amin Oueslati; Noam Kolt
summary: Analyses how the EU AI Act — promulgated before agentic AI became widespread — faces significant obstacles addressing governance challenges specific to agents: autonomous task failure, malicious misuse, and unequal liability distribution.

title: Agentic Interpretability: A Strategy Against Gradual Disempowerment
creators: beenkim
summary: AlignmentForum post by Kim, Hewitt, Nanda et al. proposing agentic interpretability as a mitigation strategy for gradual disempowerment.

title: LLM Agents Grounded in Self-Reports Enable General-Purpose Simulation of Individuals
creators: Joon Sung Park; Carolyn Q. Zou; Aaron Shaw; Benjamin Mako Hill; Carrie Cai; Meredith Ringel Morris; Robb Willer; Percy Liang; Michael S. Bernstein
tags: Persona Extraction; Simulation and Digital Twins
summary: Builds person-specific generative agents grounded in interview and survey self-report data from 1,052 Americans, achieving 83-86% of test-retest consistency and supporting general-purpose individual simulation.

title: Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI
creators: Lewis Hammond; Alan Chan; Jesse Clifton; Jason Hoelscher-Obermaier; Akbir Khan; Euan McLean; Chandler Smith; Iyad Rahwan
summary: Provides a structured taxonomy of multi-agent AI risks, identifying three key failure modes (miscoordination, conflict, collusion) and seven risk factors. Foundational survey for the field.

title: LLM economicus? Mapping the Behavioral Biases of LLMs via Utility Theory
creators: Jillian Ross; Yoon Kim; Andrew W. Lo
summary: Uses utility theory to map and quantify economic behavioral biases (loss aversion, inequity aversion, time discounting) in LLMs, finding they are neither fully human-like nor fully rational agents.

title: AI-driven disinformation: policy recommendations for democratic resilience
creators: Romanishyn, Alexander
summary: Argues AI-enabled generative and engagement-optimisation tools amplify disinformation, eroding trust and polarising democratic decision-making; proposes policy fixes.

title: Correlated Errors in Large Language Models
summary: Evaluates 350+ LLMs on leaderboards and a hiring task, finding errors are highly correlated across models sharing architecture or provider.

title: An Economy of AI Agents
creators: Gillian K. Hadfield; Andrew Koh
summary: Surveys how AI agents might interact with humans and each other, shape markets and organizations, and what institutions might be required for well-functioning markets in a future with widespread agentic deployment.

title: ABIDES: Towards High-Fidelity Market Simulation for AI Research
creators: David Byrd; Maria Hybinette; Tucker Hybinette Balch
summary: Open-source discrete-event financial market simulator supporting tens of thousands of interacting trading agents against an exchange agent.

title: Institutional AI: A Governance Framework for Distributional AGI Safety
creators: Federico Pierucci; Marcello Galisai; Marcantonio Syrnikov Bracale; Matteo Prandi; Piercosma Bisconti; Francesco Giarrusso; Olga Sorokoletova; Vincenzo Suriani
summary: Argues alignment must address agents embedded in social/technical systems, identifying structural failure modes like goal-independence and instrumental override.

title: Group size effects and collective misalignment in LLM multi-agent systems
creators: Ariel Flint; Luca Maria Aiello; Romualdo Pastor-Satorras; Andrea Baronchelli
tags: Large Agent Alignment; Emergent Harms and Capabilities
summary: Systematically shows that group size shapes collective bias in LLM multi-agent systems in non-linear, model-dependent ways — interaction can amplify, introduce, or override individual biases, with deterministic dynamics above a critical population size.
institutions: City St George's, University of London

title: Open Problems in Cooperative AI
creators: Allan Dafoe; Edward Hughes; Yoram Bachrach; Tantum Collins; Kevin R. McKee; Joel Z. Leibo; Kate Larson; Thore Graepel
summary: Dafoe et al. propose a research agenda for equipping AI systems with cooperative capabilities across cooperation problems from small to global scale.

title: GovSim: Governance of the Commons Simulation
summary: GitHub repo for GovSim, a benchmark simulating LLM agents managing shared resources under sustainability/commons-governance pressure.

title: OpenAI and Hugging Face partner to address security incident during model evaluation
summary: OpenAI/Hugging Face joint report on a security incident during model evaluation, involving advanced cyber capabilities and lessons for defenders.

title: AI as Decision-Maker: Ethics and Risk Preferences of LLMs
creators: Shumiao Ouyang; Hayong Yun; Xingjian Zheng
summary: Analyzes 50 LLMs' risk preferences in decision tasks; finds alignment tuning for harmlessness/honesty causally increases risk aversion, affecting economic forecasts.

title: Synthetic Personalities: How Well Can LLMs Mimic Individual Respondents Using Socio-Economic Microdata?
creators: Leonard Kinzinger; Jochen Hartmann
summary: Evaluates how well LLMs can mimic individual survey respondents when grounded in socio-economic microdata, assessing fidelity of synthetic personalities against real respondent data.

title: Gradual Disempowerment: Systemic Existential Risks from Incremental AI Development
creators: Jan Kulveit; Raymond Douglas; Nora Ammann; Deger Turan; David Krueger; David Duvenaud
summary: Develops the concept of gradual disempowerment — how incremental AI advances could permanently undermine human influence over the economy, culture, and nation-states without any single catastrophic event.

title: Emergent Coordination in Multi-Agent Language Models
creators: Christoph Riedl
summary: Information-theoretic framework (partial information decomposition) detecting emergent higher-order structure in multi-agent LLM systems.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Systemic Risk: A Unified Model of Performative Prediction, Algorithmic Herding, and Cognitive Dependency in Financial Markets
creators: Shuchen Meng; Xupeng Chen
summary: Meng & Chen (2026) model AI-driven systemic risk in financial markets, showing the systemic risk multiplier grows superlinearly with AI adoption share.

title: AgentSociety: Large-Scale Simulation of LLM-Driven Generative Agents Advances Understanding of Human Behaviors and Society
creators: Jinghua Piao; Yuwei Yan; Jun Zhang; Nian Li; Junbo Yan; Xiaochong Lan; Yong Li
summary: Proposes AgentSociety, a large-scale simulator integrating LLM-driven agents with a realistic societal environment, generating social lives for over 10k agents with 5 million interactions for generative social science research.

title: Intelligent AI Delegation
creators: Nenad Tomasev; Matija Franklin; Simon Osindero
summary: Proposes an adaptive framework for intelligent AI delegation, addressing task allocation, authority transfer, accountability, and trust establishment in complex multi-agent delegation networks.

title: New Report Analysing Multi-Agent Risks
creators: Gradient Institute
summary: Gradient Institute report analysing risks as organisations shift AI deployments from single agents toward multi-agent systems.

title: A Taxonomy of Systemic Risks from General-Purpose AI
creators: Risto Uuk; Carlos Ignacio Gutierrez; Daniel Guppy; Lode Lauwaert; Atoosa Kasirzadeh; Lucia Velasco; Peter Slattery; Carina Prunkl
summary: Systematic review of 86 papers proposing a taxonomy of 13 categories and 50 sources of large-scale societal/economic systemic risk from general-purpose AI.

title: AI Organizations are More Effective but Less Aligned than Individual Agents
creators: Judy Hanwen Shen
summary: Experimentally demonstrates that multi-agent 'AI organizations' achieve higher business utility but produce systematically greater misalignment than single aligned agents, across consultancy and software development tasks.

title: zkLLM: Zero Knowledge Proofs for Large Language Models
creators: Haochen Sun; Jason Li; Hongyang Zhang
summary: Presents the first specialised zero-knowledge proof system for LLMs, enabling cryptographic verification of inference correctness without revealing model parameters — foundational infrastructure for accountable agent systems.

title: Can Artificial Intelligence Enhance Corporate Financial Risk-Taking Capacity? A Perspective on Innovation Resilience and the Environment
creators: Kelin Du; Yubing Wei; Shanyue Jin
summary: Examines whether and how artificial intelligence adoption enhances corporate financial risk-taking capacity, framed through the lenses of innovation resilience and environmental sustainability.

title: Validation is the central challenge for generative social simulation: a critical review of LLMs in agent-based modeling
creators: Larooij, Maik
summary: Systematic review of generative LLM-based agent-based social simulations, mapping validation practices and arguing empirical grounding/calibration remain unresolved.

title: A global comparison of social media bot and human characteristics
creators: Ng, Lynnette Hui Xian
summary: Empirical study finding social-media chatter is ~20% bots with distinct linguistic and network-structure signatures vs. humans.

title: AgentScope 1.0: A Developer-Centric Framework for Building Agentic Applications
creators: Dawei Gao; Zitao Li; Yuexiang Xie; Weirui Kuang; Liuyi Yao; Bingchen Qian; Zhijian Ma; Yue Cui; Haohao Luo; Shen Li; Lu Yi; Yi Yu; Shiqi He; Zhiling Luo; Wenmeng Zhou; Zhicheng Zhang; Xuguang He; Ziqian Chen; Weikai Liao; Farruh Isakulovich Kushnazarov; Yaliang Li; Bolin Ding; Jingren Zhou
tags: Simulation and Digital Twins; LA Infrastructure & Protocols
summary: Presents AgentScope 1.0, a developer-centric framework for building agentic applications, supporting multi-agent simulation, orchestration, and deployment at scale.

title: Agent Drift: Quantifying Behavioral Degradation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems Over Extended Interactions
creators: Abhishek Rath
summary: Introduces 'agent drift' -- semantic, coordination, and behavioral degradation of multi-agent LLM systems over long interaction sequences -- with a theoretical framework.

title: Frontier AI Regulation: Managing Emerging Risks to Public Safety
creators: Markus Anderljung; Joslyn Barnhart; Anton Korinek; Jade Leung; Cullen O'Keefe; Jess Whittlestone; Shahar Avin; Miles Brundage
summary: Anderljung et al. propose regulatory building blocks (standards, licensing, monitoring) for frontier AI models with dangerous capabilities.
institutions: Centre for the Governance of AI

title: GitHub - lechmazur/emergent_collusion: Systemic, uninstructed collusion among frontier LLMs in a simulated bidding environment
summary: Repo documenting uninstructed, systemic price-fixing collusion emerging among frontier LLM agents in a simulated auction/bidding environment.

title: AI swarms are starting to pose indirect takeover risk
creators: oakhu
summary: Alignment Forum post arguing OpenAI's Hugging Face breach resulted from many agents coordinating across distinct contexts, posing indirect takeover risk.

title: SocioVerse: A World Model for Social Simulation Powered by LLM Agents and A Pool of 10 Million Real-World Users
summary: SocioVerse: an LLM-agent 'world model' for social simulation grounded in profiles of 10 million real users, enabling large-scale social behavior simulation.

title: Modeling Earth-Scale Human-Like Societies with One Billion Agents
creators: Haoxiang Guan; Jiyan He; Liyang Fan; Zhenzhen Ren; Shaobin He; Shuxin Zheng; Zhen Liu
summary: Presents Light Society, an agent-based simulation framework that advances LLM-powered simulation to planetary scale (one billion agents), formalising social processes as structured state transitions executed through an event queue.

title: Distributional AGI Safety
creators: Nenad Tomasev; Matija Franklin; Julian Jacobs; Simon Krier; Simon Osindero
summary: Develops the concept of distributional AGI — emergent collective intelligence arising from large populations of agents — and proposes defence-in-depth mechanisms including cryptographic identity, market design, and accountability infrastructure.

title: Detecting Multi-Agent Collusion Through Multi-Agent Interpretability
creators: Aaron Rose
summary: Introduces NARCBench and five activation-based probing techniques for detecting covert multi-agent collusion, achieving 1.00 AUROC in-distribution and strong zero-shot transfer across structurally diverse scenarios.

title: Automation and Repression
creators: Daron Acemoglu; A. Arda Gitmez; Mehdi Shadmehr
tags: Threat Models; Labour & Automation; Policy and Governance
summary: Models automation embedded in a political environment where workers can revolt; decentralised automation raises capital's income share and the likelihood of successful revolt. Shows a complementarity between automation and political repression: capitalist states facing AI-driven inequality may find repression cheaper than redistribution as automation increases.

title: Language models transmit behavioural traits through hidden signals in data
summary: Cloud, Le, Chua et al. (Nature) show 'subliminal learning': a student LLM distilled on a teacher's semantically-unrelated number sequences still absorbs the teacher's behavioural traits.

title: The Moltbook Observatory Archive: an incremental dataset of agent-only social network activity
creators: Sushant Gautam; Annika W. Olstad; Klas H. Pettersen; Michael A. Riegler
summary: Presents the Moltbook Observatory Archive, an incremental dataset passively recording agent profiles, posts, comments, community metadata, platform-level snapshots, and word-frequency trends from Moltbook, an AI-agent-only social media platform.
institutions: Simula Metropolitan Center for Digital Engineering (SimulaMet)

title: AI Agents Under EU Law: A Compliance Architecture for AI Providers
creators: Luca Nannini; Adam Leon Smith; Michele Joshua Maggini; Enrico Panai; Sandra Feliciano; Aleksandr Tiulkanov; Elena Maran; James Gealy; Piercosma Bisconti
summary: First systematic regulatory mapping for AI agent providers under EU law (AI Act, GDPR, CRA, DSA, NIS2), proposing a twelve-step compliance architecture and regulatory trigger mapping connecting agent actions to applicable legislation.

title: Agentic Microphysics: A Manifesto for Generative AI Safety
creators: Federico Pierucci; M. Galisai; M. Bracale; M. Prandi; P. Bisconti
tags: Emergent Harms and Capabilities; Foundations & Taxonomies
summary: Proposes 'agentic microphysics' as a level of analysis (local interaction dynamics between agents) and 'generative safety' as a methodology for growing emergent risks from micro-level conditions to identify intervention points.

title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
creators: Mert Cemri; Melissa Z. Pan; Shuyi Yang; Lakshya A. Agrawal; Bhavya Chopra; Rishabh Tiwari; Kurt Keutzer; Aditya Parameswaran
summary: Builds MAST, the first Multi-Agent System failure taxonomy, from 1600+ annotated traces across 7 MAS frameworks to explain poor MAS performance.

title: Virtual Agent Economies
creators: Nenad Tomasev; Matija Franklin; Joel Z. Leibo; Julian Jacobs; William A. Cunningham; Iason Gabriel; Simon Osindero
summary: Proposes the 'sandbox economy' framework for analysing the emergent AI agent economic layer. Covers auction mechanisms, mission economies, and conditions for safely steerable AI agent markets.
